page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-16GB is a shared-core cloud compute instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The virtual machine is configured with 8 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Standard CPU instruction extensions include AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, while newer AVX-512 and matrix extensions are unsupported. This instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes, and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results show mixed compute performance reflecting its shared CPU allocation. Synthetic stress-ng evaluations place single-core and multi-core throughput in lower percentiles. In contrast, standard architectural benchmarks such as Geekbench demonstrate strong single-core performance with a score of 2027.0 and average multi-core throughput reaching 10101.0. Memory subsystem throughput benchmarks, including uncached read speeds of 30.23 GB/s and write speeds of 17.66 GB/s, place the memory bus in the lower tier relative to dedicated compute hardware.

Application and operational metrics indicate balanced capacity for general processing tasks. The instance delivers 11.14 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and sustained throughput in software compilation benchmarks. However, memory-intensive execution and larger LLM inference workloads display noticeable constraints due to limited memory bandwidth and lack of vector accelerators.

UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-16GB functions effectively as a cost-efficient resource for containerized microservices, build nodes, CI/CD pipeline agents, and web application runtimes where predictable compute bursting is acceptable and high-speed local disk I/O is not required.

It serves adequately for distributed web serving, continuous integration runners, lightweight compilation tasks, and containerized microservices.
